MCP mass decomposition from ion m/z

Source: R/chemform_decompose.R
chemform_decompose_mz.Rd

Convert ion m/z + charge to neutral exact mass (same electron-mass convention as chemform_mz()), then call chemform_decompose_mass().

Usage

chemform_decompose_mz(
  mz,
  charge = 0,
  ppm = 5,
  mzabs = 1e-04,
  elements = c("C", "H", "N", "O", "P", "S"),
  min_elements = NULL,
  max_elements = NULL,
  check_rule = FALSE
)

Arguments

mz

Ion m/z (scalar or vector). If charge = 0, treated as neutral mass.

charge

Integer charge z (e.g. +1, +2, -1). Use 0 for neutral input.

ppm

Allowed deviation in ppm (applied on the neutral mass used for MCP).

mzabs

Allowed absolute deviation in Dalton.

elements

Character vector of allowed elements.

min_elements

See chemform_decompose_mass().

max_elements

See chemform_decompose_mass().

check_rule

If TRUE, keep only candidates that pass chemform_check_seven_golden_rules() (passed through to chemform_decompose_mass()). Default FALSE. Disabled automatically when any min_elements count is negative (see chemform_decompose_mass()).

Value

A data.frame with columns formula, exactmass, mz, ppm, charge, and mz_target. Rows are sorted by increasing abs(ppm) vs the input m/z.

Details

Neutral mass conversion when charge != 0: M = mz * abs(charge) + e * charge, with e = 0.00054857990943.

See also

chemform_decompose_mass(), chemform_mz(), chemform_check_seven_golden_rules()
